title: Make an expiry check explain its refusals in the log

blocks.text: The support desk has a run of tickets about cards refused with `54` (expired card), and a few with `30`, from cardholders whose cards are valid until next year. The server's log has the TransactionManager's events and nothing else: `prepare: c.e.p.CardExpiry ABORTED`. Nobody can tell which expiry date the server read, or which month it compared it with.
Write `prepare` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/CardExpiry.java`. `refusal` already decides and `reply` builds the answer: `54` for an expired card, `30` for an expiry that can't be read.

When you're done, an operator who has a terminal ID and a STAN finds in the log one entry for every purchase this participant handled, whether it let it through, refused it, or couldn't read it, with what it decided and why. From that entry the operator can find the TransactionManager's event for the same transaction. The log is shipped to a platform that a few hundred people can search. About 15 lines.

The tests call the participant directly. They give it a logger whose chain is the production one, `ProtectedLogListener` and then a writer, the way `logger="Q2" realm="card-expiry"` would under Q2. The current month is fixed at November 2026.

cases.says: a card that has not expired is not refused and gets no response from this participant
an expired card is answered 54, and one event in the participant's realm shows the purchase and the expiry it read
an expiry that can't be read is answered 30 and still leaves its one event, because the event is written whatever happened
a purchase the participant lets through leaves an event as well, not only the refusals
the request goes into the event as a message, so the filter masks it; the Context, which dumps the request in clear, does not
each transaction gets a new event, because one participant instance serves every transaction
logging leaves the request and the response as they are; masking is the filter's job, on its own copy
the event carries the transaction id, which joins it to the TransactionManager's event for the same transaction

origin.section: 8.3 One Event per Transaction, Carrying Its Id and the Message Itself

concepts: A participant writes one event per transaction, created in prepare, with the transaction id, the request as a message for the filter to mask, and the reason, logged in finally whatever happened.
